aiOverview.content: "#SKYKING: Panic in the Sky" is a 2026 ABC News Studios documentary premiering April 14 on Hulu and Disney+, detailing the August 10, 2018, theft of a Horizon Air Q400 plane by ground agent Richard "Beebo" Russell. Russell performed unauthorized aerobatic maneuvers over Puget Sound, including a barrel roll, for 70 minutes before crashing on Ketron Island. The film explores the psychological, tragic, and surreal aspects of the incident through air traffic control audio and interviews.Key Details of the 2018 IncidentThe Perpetrator: Richard "Beebo" Russell, a 29-year-old ground service agent for Horizon Air, who was described as a "broken guy" in recordings, with no intention of hurting others but seeking to end his own life.The Aircraft: A Horizon Air De Havilland Dash 8-400 turboprop (valued at $33 million) was stolen from Seattle-Tacoma International Airport.The Flight: Russell flew for roughly 70–75 minutes, performing reckless maneuvers, including a barrel roll and flying upside down, while communicating with air traffic control.The Response: Two F-15 Eagle fighter jets were scrambled to intercept the plane, creating a sonic boom in the process, but they did not fire upon it.The Crash: The aircraft crashed on Ketron Island, southwest of Tacoma, resulting in the death of Russell.Documentary FeaturesRelease Date: April 14, 2026.Platform: Streaming on Hulu and Disney+.Focus: The documentary, directed by P.E. Gillespie, focuses on the human story behind the headlines, including interviews with family, friends, and the air traffic controller, Colleen, who managed the crisis.The documentary, which is also referred to as simply #SKYKING or SkyKing, delves into the "why" behind the incident, touching upon mental health and the limitations of airport security, according to ABC News Studios' Instagram and Fox13 Seattle.
